title: A cancelled delegated child keeps its runtime and MCP server processes alive, with cwd inside the delegating worktree, which blocks worktree removal
outcome: When a delegated child is cancelled or finishes, TermAl ends that child's runtime and the MCP server processes it started (termal.exe delegation-mcp and engram.exe mcp for that child session), so no process keeps a cwd or handle inside the delegating worktree. Alternatively, child MCP servers are started with a cwd outside the worktree. A cancelled child leaves no running process. Tests cover cancel before any command, cancel mid-turn, and normal finish. The process cleanup guarantees in this item apply to Windows; Unix launch and cleanup behavior remain unchanged, and this item makes no Unix descendant-cleanup guarantee.
acceptance: Before the product correction, reproduce the reported cancellation leak and finished-control-sidecar worktree pin with deterministic owned-process regressions through the public lifecycle paths; preserve the failing output and classify each cause. Fixtures and stores stay under repository .tmp, and no manual process kill or host restart supplies the asserted cleanup.

On Windows, canceling a delegated child through the public cancel route releases that child's runtime ownership and terminates its child-specific runtime/MCP subprocesses and descendants, including TermAl delegation-mcp and Engram mcp where configured. Tests cover cancellation before the first command and during an active turn, and verify actual process exit rather than only local status or runtime-map removal. A shared app-server serving other sessions may remain running, but it retains no canceled-child MCP process or handle in the delegating worktree. Verify with host-recorded process-lifecycle regression checks at the judged source revision.

On Windows, a normally completed or failed delegated child releases its child-specific runtime/MCP resources, and its host-managed Engram control sidecar cannot keep a cwd or handle inside the delegating worktree while awaiting idle reaping. Preserve the explicit project, store and session authority when changing sidecar cwd. Real-process regressions demonstrate prompt removal of an otherwise empty disposable worktree directory after cancellation and normal completion, without waiting for the idle timeout or restarting TermAl. Verify with host-recorded process-lifecycle regression checks at the judged source revision.

Cleanup remains scoped to the terminal child: concurrently active children and sessions sharing its app-server continue to operate, normal completed-child follow-up/release behavior remains valid, and cancellation preserves existing durable Engram observation/grant recovery duties. Failed or ambiguous cleanup remains diagnosable and retains the ownership needed for safe retry; it must not be reported as confirmed process exit. Verify with host-recorded lifecycle and recovery regression checks at the judged source revision.

The maintained five-stage full gate passes on the exact final source input, compiled from that input, with its host verification recorded before independent acceptance evaluation. The independent Codex/Claude read-only review pair has no unresolved in-scope Medium or higher finding on that same input.
